prompt:
You are a grounded brand-outreach assistant for our team. Use only the evidence passages below.
Never use outside knowledge. Return valid JSON only.

Separate three things:
1. OBSERVED FACTS - things a passage actually states about this company. Each fact is a claim with an id (C1, C2, ...),
   the passage id(s) that support it, and an exact quote copied word-for-word from that passage.
2. UNKNOWNS - things the evidence does not tell us (put them in "unknowns"). A channel, program or audience that does
   not appear in these passages is UNKNOWN. It is never a weakness, never a "gap", and never a reason for outreach.
3. PROPOSALS - collaboration ideas from our team. Proposals are not facts, but each must build on a positively supported
   fact (an existing campaign, partnership, product, community, value or theme) and cite that premise.

Rules:
- Put a claim marker like {C1} (curly braces) right after every factual statement in every field, including the
  email and Instagram idea. Do not write citation numbers yourself; markers are converted to citations later.
- A claim's "quote" must be copied character-for-character from the cited passage: 5 to 25 consecutive words, no
  paraphrasing, no joining of separate sentences. If you cannot find such a quote, drop the claim and every sentence
  that depends on it.
- Audience and strategy sentences are factual: each needs a marker. If no passage states the audience, write
  INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE instead of guessing.
- Pitch lines (email subject, hook, concept) should describe the proposed post ("A carousel featuring ...",
  "Collaborate on ..."). Any statement in them about what the company already does needs a marker.
- Respect passage types. "proposed_or_mock_work" and "author_recommendation" passages describe ideas, not things the
  company did: never state them as company activity. "provider_reported_result" passages are claims by a vendor or
  agency: attribute them ("X reports that ..."). "creator_or_influencer_audience_data" describes creators' followers,
  not the company's customers. "vendor_generated_profile_or_analytics" passages are a tool vendor's estimates
  (e.g. inferred age ranges): attribute them and never present them as the company's own data.
  "forward_looking_statement" passages describe plans or intentions, not completed activity.
- Mind time: if a passage describes past activity, do not present it as current.
- "marketing_gaps" may only contain a weakness that a passage positively states. Usually it is [].
- Never promise results. Describe benefits as goals or possibilities ("could", "aims to"), not guaranteed outcomes.
- Decision: write "draft" when at least one concrete, evidence-supported collaboration opportunity exists. Otherwise write
  "abstain", give an abstain_reason, set pitch fields to INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE and leave collaboration_opportunities empty.
- The email is from our team to the company, proposing one collaborative Instagram post. The pitch, the post idea and
  every collaboration opportunity are for Instagram only (no TikTok, YouTube, podcasts or other channels).
- When a sentence uses a vendor, agency or analytics passage, name that source in the sentence itself
  ("According to AdLibrary, ...", "Attentive reports that ...").
- Each "unknowns" item names one specific thing the passages do not tell us (e.g. "Whether X runs a creator program").
  Never write placeholder text such as "what the evidence does not show".

Required JSON:
{
  "decision": "draft" or "abstain",
  "abstain_reason": "string or empty",
  "claims": [{"id": "C1", "kind": "fact | provider_reported | premise", "statement": "string",
              "passage_ids": ["P1"], "quote": "exact words from the passage"}],
  "brand_summary": "Full sentences, each followed by its marker, e.g. "X makes ... {C1}." Never only markers. Or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE",
  "likely_target_audience": "A full sentence followed by its marker, or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE",
  "current_marketing_strategy": ["text with markers"],
  "unknowns": ["one specific open question, e.g. Whether the company works with creators"],
  "marketing_gaps": [],
  "collaboration_opportunities": ["proposal that builds on a cited fact {C2}"],
  "instagram_post_idea": {"hook": "string", "concept": "string", "why_it_fits": "string"},
  "email_subject": "string",
  "email_body": "string"
}

Company: Burrow (company_id burrow; category: modular furniture)
Official domains: burrow.com
Recipient: the marketing team
Packet status: ok

Evidence passages:
[P1] source: https://burrow.com/about | document: official_domain | type: brand_positioning | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"So we made it modular, designed it to do more, and got it to your door in days. Because we believe great design isn’t just how it looks. It’s how it works. couple relaxing and laughing on a Burrow sofa SMARTER IN EVERY WAY"

[P2] source: https://burrow.com/about | document: official_domain | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Innovation you can actually feel We design every piece to work harder and make life easier—from fast delivery and seamless assembly to modular flexibility and thoughtful features like hidden chargers and performance fabrics. The result? Clever solutions for every corner of your home. shipping truck icon SPEED OF DELIVERY Styles that arrive to your home in as little as a week. modular furniture icon ENHANCED FUNCTIONALITY Modular and clever, it’s easier than ever to move. durable icon wine spilling on fabrid DURABLE MATERIALS Strong frames and performance fabrics built to last. plush cushion icon SERIOUSLY COMFORTABLE From supportive to sink-in, cushions for every kind of lounge."

[P3] source: https://www.casestudies.com/company/pepperjam/case-study/burrow-assembles-the-perfect-customer-acquisition-strategy-with-diversified-affiliate-approach | document: third_party_confirmed | type: actual_activity | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Burrow assembles the perfect customer acquisition strategy with diversified affiliate approach Burrow, a direct-to-consumer furniture brand, needed to reach new audiences and convert shoppers while avoiding high acquisition costs from paid search, social, and traditional PR. To diversify its marketing mix, Burrow partnered with Pepperjam and used the Pepperjam Ascend™ platform to tap partner distribution through a scalable, pay-for-performance affiliate approach. Using Pepperjam’s Ascend™ (with Discover technology), Burrow identified and recruited right-fit partners, automated lookalike recommendations, and optimized creative assets to converge brand and performance marketing."

[P4] source: https://adlibrary.com/brands/burrow | document: third_party_confirmed | type: provider_reported_result | flags: vendor_generated_profile_or_analytics | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Browse Burrow's Facebook and Instagram ad creatives at adlibrary.com?q=Burrow&type=3. What platforms does Burrow advertise on? Burrow advertises on Facebook and Instagram, with YouTube influencer partnerships and Google Shopping supplementing direct-response paid social. Who are Burrow's main competitors? Competitors include Floyd, Joybird, West Elm, and Pottery Barn in the modular and DTC sofa category. What makes Burrow's ads effective? Burrow's assembly demonstration videos directly neutralize the biggest sofa purchase anxiety — delivery and setup complexity — by showing the entire process takes minutes without tools, making the purchase feel risk-free. Does Burrow have physical stores?"

[P5] source: https://adlibrary.com/brands/burrow | document: third_party_confirmed | type: author_recommendation | flags: vendor_generated_profile_or_analytics | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Burrow Google Ads, YouTube Ads & Cross-Platform Lessons Burrow solved a logistics problem (sofa delivery in apartment buildings) and made that solution the centerpiece of its marketing. The lesson: when a product feature solves a genuine friction point that competitors haven't addressed, that feature should be the ad's hero. Burrow also demonstrates how modular product architecture enables upsell ad sequences — existing customers are the highest-converting audience for 'add a piece' campaigns."

[P6] source: https://burrow.com/about | document: official_domain | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"THE SPAN SLEEPER Designed for those who want it all We took a real queen-sized mattress and turned it into the stylish sleeper sofa of your dreams."

[P7] source: https://adlibrary.com/brands/burrow | document: third_party_confirmed | type: provider_reported_result | flags: vendor_generated_profile_or_analytics | dates in text: 2016 | published: unknown
"About Burrow Burrow was founded in New York in 2016 by Kabeer Chopra and Stephen Kuhl, launching a tool-free modular sofa that ships in regular-sized boxes and assembles in minutes. The configuration system allows buyers to add arms, chaises, and sections over time. Burrow has since expanded into full-room furniture with shelving, coffee tables, and rugs, opening physical showrooms in key markets while maintaining a DTC-first pricing model."

generator.quote_repair: claims.repair_quotes (min similarity 0.9; numbers/negations unchanged); see attempts[].quote_repairs
generator.note: repair rounds show the teacher only its own draft and the failed check messages
